title_en: The Indispensable Preliminaries to the Science of Creed
body_ar:
قبل الشروع في أي علم ينبغي أن يعرف الطالب مقدماته العشر التي بمعرفتها يسهل التعلم، وهذه المبادئ العشر اهتم أهل العلم ببيانها وشرحها لطلاب العلم، ومن أهم ذلك مقدمات علم العقائد.
معرفة حد علم العقائد:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، والصلاة والسلام على سيد الأنبياء والمرسلين، نبينا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه أجمعين. قبل الشروع في كل علم ينبغي أن يطلع الإنسان على عشر مقدمات يحتاج إليها في تصور ذلك العلم الذي يريد الإقدام على تعلمه، وهذه المقدمات العشر هي التي نظمها المقري بقوله: من رام فناً فليقـــدم أولاً ***علماً بحده وموضـوع تلا/ وواضع، ونسبة وما استمــد *** منه، وفضله، وحكم يعتمـد/ واسم وما أفاد والمســائل *** فتلك عشر للمنى وسـائل/ وبعضهم فيها على البعض اقتصر*** ومن يكن يدري جميعها انتصر...
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* Before embarking on any science, the student ought to know its ten preliminaries, by the knowledge of which learning is made easier. The people of knowledge have taken care to set out and explain these ten principles for students of knowledge; and among the most important of them are the preliminaries to the science of creed.

## Knowing the definition of the science of creed

In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Mercy-Giving. Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds, and blessing and peace upon the master of the prophets and the messengers, our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and his Companions all together. Before embarking on any science, a person ought to acquaint himself with ten preliminaries which he needs in order to form a conception of the science he intends to set about learning. These ten preliminaries are the ones al-Maqqari put into verse, saying:

*Whoever aims at a discipline, let him put first a knowledge of its definition, and its subject matter next; and its founder, and its relation to other sciences, and the sources it draws upon, and its merit, and the ruling (ḥukm) relied upon concerning it; and its name, and what it yields, and its questions. Those are ten, and they are the means to what is sought. Some have confined themselves to a part of them; but whoever knows them all has prevailed.*

flags.context: the record breaks off and the full text sits behind a download
options: render with an excerpt banner and link the .doc
flags.note: Excerpt only, style guide section 9. It breaks off on an ellipsis at the end of the cited verses, so that the ten preliminaries are named in verse and not one of them is expounded — including the definition of the science of creed, which is the subject of the section heading. The complete text sits behind /medias/doc/L-31.doc. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends and completes nothing. Must not be rendered as a whole lesson.

flags.arabic: الفقرة الافتتاحية مقابل ما بعد العنوان الفرعي
flags.context: the synopsis paragraph against the transcribed opening of the lesson
options: mark the synopsis as the site's own and the remainder as the Sheikh's words
present the whole record as the Sheikh's words
flags.note: The record has two authors. The first paragraph is a synopsis written by the site — it speaks about the lesson and its subject in the third person and does not begin with the opening formula. Everything from the section heading onward is transcribed speech in the Sheikh's own voice. The site must not present the synopsis as his words.

options: The Preliminaries Known by Immediate Necessity
flags.note: A homonym that inverts the sense if taken wrongly. In kalām and logic 'ضروري' is a technical term for knowledge that is immediate and not acquired by inference — and this is a record about kalām, which makes the technical reading tempting. It is not the sense here: the synopsis and the opening sentence both gloss the word by saying the student 'ought to know' these ten things before starting, which is indispensability, not immediacy. 'Indispensable' has been chosen over 'necessary' precisely to keep the technical reading out. Note also that 'ضرورة' in the glossary is the legal threshold of necessity, a third sense again, and not in play here either.

flags.context: the seventh of the ten preliminaries, in al-Maqqari's verse
options: the ruling (ḥukm) relied upon concerning it
the accepted legal ruling on studying it
flags.note: This item is the legal ruling on occupying oneself with the science — whether studying it is individually obligatory, communally obligatory, recommended, and so on. The verse names the item without giving the ruling, and the excerpt breaks off before the Sheikh states it for the science of creed. The English must therefore name the category and supply no ruling, which is what it does. A reader must not be left thinking a ruling has been given.

options: the definition of the science of creed
the scope of the science of creed
the limit of the science of creed
flags.note: 'حد' in this register is the logicians' term for a real definition by genus and differentia, and it is the first of the ten preliminaries in the verse that follows. 'Definition' is right; 'limit' or 'scope' would break the correspondence with the verse.

flags.context: the attribution of the cited verses
options: keep the attribution exactly as given
expand to identify which al-Maqqari is meant
flags.note: The Sheikh names 'المقري' and nothing further. The name is borne by more than one scholar, and these well-travelled verses on the ten principles are attributed variously in the literature. The attribution is reproduced exactly as given, without expansion and without a date, per style guide section 4.

translator_notes: One of a run of fifteen records, IDs 707-721, in the written-creed section, all uploaded on 9 and 10 May 2011 within a few hours of one another, all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and the first lines of a lesson, and then breaks off on an ellipsis; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/L-* series, numbered L-26 to L-39 in the same order as the IDs. The uniform timestamps are a bulk upload and say nothing about when the lesson was delivered.

The record contains two distinct voices and the English keeps them apart. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, about the lesson and in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the Sheikh's own words as transcribed. Nothing in the synopsis may be quoted as his.

The source's final line, 'تحميل المادة' ('download the material'), is the label of a download link in the page furniture, not part of the text. It is recorded as source_download_link and omitted from body_ar and body_en.

The verses are rendered as continuous prose in italics per style guide section 4; the source's hemistich markers (*** and /) are kept in body_ar and not carried into the English. No rhymed English has been attempted.
The record is almost entirely quotation: after the opening formula the Sheikh gives two sentences of his own and then recites four lines of verse, at which point the text stops.
No ruling term from the five-rulings table appears anywhere in the record. The verse names the category of the ruling as one of the ten preliminaries but states no ruling.
